newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Gerry Kiely briefed on next week's Farm Council in Luxembourg. He said the aim was to reach a conclusion at least on measures having immediate impact on production of beef and beef products by Wednesday morning.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida briefed on next week's General Affairs Council. He said there should be joint EU action to help the electoral process in Zaire. He also said the recent developments in the Great Lakes Region would be discussed and that the EU would try to create the conditions for dialogue between the parties in conflict.

Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said the delays in the elections in ex-Yugoslavia, the need to reinforce the role of the high representative to Bosnia, the structured dialogue with the Central and Eastern European Countries and the relations with Turkey would also be discussed during the council.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said that the trade issues to be discussed during the council would be the U.S. Helms-Burton Act, the Singapore World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting, the negotiating mandate for an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) and the WTO telecoms negotiations. He also said the EU hoped to sign an EU-Korea framework agreement during the special council with Korea.

Spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the ministers would also discuss EU relations with Egypt in the scope of a potential Euro Mediterranean Associations Agreement. EU and Egypt will also discuss the peace process in the Middle-East, he said.

In answer to a question spokesmen Nikolaus van der Pas and Peter Guilford denied the impression left by a recent speach by Commissioner Leon Brittan that the Commission was criticizing France's parallel political action in the Middle-East.
